range.description:
Simple value filter; the values are directly compared to the specified min/max. Note that for a useful filter, the
max value should be larger than the min (when both are specified).

stddev.description:
Standard-deviation filter. If a single value is provided, the same number of standard deviations above and below
the mean are filtered. If a range is provided, the min and max may be different. If specified the min/max should
be positive and the bounds will be: _mean_ ± _stddev.min_ σ.

For example: `{ stddev: 2 }` would remove points 2 standard deviations above and below the mean while
`{ stddev: { min: 3, max: 2 }` would remove points 3 standard deviations above and 2 below the mean.

percentile.description:
Percentile rank range in [1..99]. For example `{ percentile: { min: 10, max: 90 }` would filter to values between
the 10th and 90 percentiles. Note that for a useful filter, the max percentile should be larger than the min
(when both are specified).

clip.description:
Clip out-of-bound values instead of removing them. This retains all (numeric) values, but adjusts them to the
declared range.

ignoreHigh.description: Ignore values that are above the range.

ignoreLow.description: Ignore values that are below the range.

title:
The options for detecting extreme values of a population based on standard statistics of that population.
All of the fields are optional, which means by default nothing will be detected. If multiple filters are specified,
_all_ must be met for a point to not match.

Having separate high and low filter ranges allows rejection of points where the population variance is not the same
at the high and low ends. For example, a tightly clustered population with occasional high outliers might benefit
from a tight high filter (say 2σ) and a loose low filter (say P₁₀), or even no low filter at all.

For example a filter for _mean_ ± 2σ would be: `{ stddev: 2 }` and a filter for positive values below
_mean_ + 3σ would be: `{ range: { min: 0, minExclusive: true }, stddev: { max: 3 } }`.

Note that instead of removing values, they may be also be clipped to the relevant bound by setting the #clip field
to `true`. For example, `{ range: { min: 0, max: 100, maxInclusive: true }, clip: true }` would convert all values
into the range [0..100] without dropping any (without maxInclusive, it would be [0..100) since max is exclusive by
default).

@see NumCollection#withoutOutliers
